subject: Transfer appendix & access boundary — follow-up
messages:
From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@medisafe.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: Legal Ops <legal-ops@medisafe.com>
Date: 2027-01-18 09:12 PST
Subject: Transfer appendix and access boundary questions

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking this — Medisafe is working through the DPA transfer annex and a couple items popped up that we need clarified before our Legal Ops signs off. Short list below: 

1) Residency: We need confirmation that any new EU subprocessor hosts customer data within EU-only regions by default, and a fallback path if capacity requires transient processing outside the EU (audit logs, justification, and data minimization).

2) Access boundary: We want concrete examples of how you segment PII in production (tokenization, metadata-only indices), and which Redwood roles can access raw PII (and via what approvals).

3) Subprocessor approval flow: If Redwood proposes a new infra subprocessor (e.g., a managed DB provider or logging vendor), what timelines and evidence do you provide? We typically require SOC2 + dataflow diagram + KMS boundary checklist.

Can you provide a short annex or attachments addressing these points and any proposed clause language? We are trying to keep the DPA timeline tight (two-week turnaround).

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Sara
Sara Jensen
Head of Legal Ops, Medisafe

From: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@medisafe.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-19 11:04 PST
Subject: Re: Transfer appendix and access boundary questions

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses inline and attachments attached (redwood-dataflow-v2.pdf + transfer-annex-draft).

1) Residency: By default, for EU customers we pin workloads to EU regions (Frankfurt / Dublin) and provision model serving and storage to EU-only clusters. In cases of transient overflow we:
  - Route to nearest compatible EU region first; if unavailable, we failover to a predefined fallback region and create an automated incident with justification.
  - We log the justification, impacted customer id(s), and retention duration in an audit bucket (EU-held where possible).
  - We can add a contract-level clause: "Redwood will not transfer or process Customer Personal Data outside the EU except for documented, temporary overflow events where Redwood has reasonably determined such processing is necessary for continuity of service; Redwood shall notify Customer within 48 hours and provide an incident justification log."

2) Access boundary & PII segmentation:
  - PII classification: fields tagged as FULL_PII in ingestion are stored in encrypted object storage with envelope encryption (KMS) separate from vector index stores.
  - Tokenization: for customers requesting de-identification we offer a tokenization pipeline (separate token store sitting in customer region).
  - Roles: access to raw PII is limited to SRE on-call and a small set of Support Engineers under break-glass with documented approvals. Approvals require 2-person review (ticket + manager signoff) and are recorded in the access log.
  - See redwood-dataflow-v2.pdf for the diagram showing tokenization, KMS boundary, and KV cache scoping.

3) Subprocessor approval flow: Proposed flow we can commit to: 
  - Notification: Redwood notifies Customer at least 30 days before onboarding a new subprocessor with name, country, purpose, and data types processed.
  - Evidence package within 5 business days: SOC2 report (or equivalent), dataflow diagram slice showing where Customer PII touches the subprocessor, and KMS/crypto boundary description.
  - Escalation: If Customer objects within 15 days, Redwood will agree to pause onboarding for the Customer’s tenant or provide an alternative configuration where feasible.

Attachments: transfer-annex-draft includes the clause language and a short SLA exception for transient overflow. Also attached: subprocessor-approval-log.csv export with recent vendor evidence.

If helpful I can loop in Product (Marcus) for any technical clarifications and Security (Neha) for the KMS attestation details — cc'ing them here. We can turn this into the DPA appendix and route for DocuSign by next week.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Privacy, Redwood Inference

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-20 08:33 PST
Subject: Re: Transfer appendix and access boundary questions

Sofia — quick internal note before we send final: two items to decide.

1) Overflow handling: Neha recommends adding a requirement that any audit log referencing a customer id in a non-EU region must be stored in an EU-locked archival bucket within 30 days (so Medisafe can demonstrate control). That adds retention overhead but is acceptable for enterprise deals.

2) Subprocessor timeline: Our standard is 30 days notice + 5 business day evidence package. Legal wants to avoid an automatic pause obligation (15 days) that could block infra improvements. Proposed compromise: allow Customer to request mitigation or pause for their tenant only (we can support tenant-level exemptions in Dedicated/Private; hosted customers get alternative config where available).

Neha — can you confirm the exact KMS attestation wording we can provide (HSM vs Cloud KMS, export restrictions)? I think we have a one-page attestation that states: keys for EU-hosted tenants remain under EU keyrings and exports are disallowed without customer consent.

Marcus

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-20 09:15 PST
Subject: Re: Transfer appendix and access boundary questions

Confirmed — we can provide the following attestation language for the annex: 

"Redwood attests that for Customer tenants configured for EU residency, cryptographic key material used for envelope encryption is provisioned into EU-region keyrings (Cloud KMS or customer-managed HSM). Redwood will not export plaintext key material outside of EU boundaries. Operational key usage logs will be retained for 90 days in an EU logging cluster; exports of those logs to non-EU regions will not occur unless required by law."

I'll attach the one-page KMS attestation and add the EU-lock archival step Marcus suggested. Once Sofia and Legal confirm, I can sign the tech attestation and we'll bundle for DocuSign.

-Neha
